ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In Figure 5, there are three circular schematic diagrams numbered ①②③. The center of each says "human society," and the periphery is "environment." In the left-right direction, exchange relationships of "material energy" and "waste" are marked. Diagram ① prominently marks "development" in the up-down direction, indicating that human society develops the environment; diagram ② marks "influence" in the up-down direction, indicating the influence of the environment on human society; diagram ③ has both "influence" and "development," indicating that the environment influences human society, while human society also develops and acts on the environment. Then reason: According to the historical evolution of human-land relationship thought, the early period emphasized the determining role of the natural environment on human society, namely environmental determinism, corresponding to ②; subsequently it emphasized humans developing and conquering nature, namely human-centered or nature-development thought, corresponding to ①; later it recognized mutual interaction between humans and land and pursued human-land coordination, corresponding to ③. Therefore, the diagram sequence that conforms to historical evolution is ②①③, namely 213.
